item.title: Lindsay Clancy trial jury resumes deliberations as mistrial potential grows
item.description: There has been a lengthy sidebar in the Lindsay Clancy murder trial in Massachusetts for an unknown reason as deliberations have surpassed 34 hours without a verdict.

item.title: Iran's attacks didn't impact military facilities used by U.S., official says
item.description: Iran responded to a warning from President Trump with claims of new strikes against U.S. forces in Kuwait and the United Arab Emirates.

item.title: CBS reporter tests London's first self-driving taxis
item.description: The first self-driving taxis have launched in London. Uber has 15 vehicles operating in the city with a required supervisor in the car. CBS News' Leigh Kiniry took an autonomous ride with Wayve co-founder and CEO Alex Kendall, whose AI technology is powering the robotaxis in London's iconic Westminster.

item.title: Watch: Vance holds White House press briefing, talks Iran and midterm elections
item.description: Vice President JD Vance on Thursday held the first White House press briefing since Karoline Leavitt departed as press secretary. Following the briefing, CBS News' Aaron Navarro provided further context.

item.title: Judge blocks Trump's latest effort to narrow birthright citizenship
item.description: A federal judge has temporarily blocked a Trump executive order that would prevent certain people from automatically becoming U.S. citizens at birth.

item.title: How much interest can a $100,000 6-month CD earn at today's rates?
item.description: A $100,000 6-month CD will provide short-term protection and a boost to your savings in 2027. Here's what to know.

item.title: DOJ reviving dormant prize law to try to claim Iranian oil tankers
item.description: The Justice Department is planning to try to use a legal regime last used during the Spanish-American War to speed up the seizure of ships and their cargo during the Iran conflict.

item.title: New testosterone guidelines temporarily rescinded, Pentagon says
item.description: The Pentagon will begin requiring male service members ages 30 and older to get screened for testosterone deficiency, after Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth called for the change over the summer.

item.title: Is a CD or a high-yield savings account better to open this September?
item.description: Not sure which savings account type is better to open this September? Here's how you can decide.

item.title: These athletes will advance to the U.S. Open's third round
item.description: The U.S. Open is underway in New York City. Sports Illustrated senior writer and 60 Minutes correspondent Jon Wertheim has the latest on tennis starts to watch.

item.title: Estrogen patch shortage prompts doctors, lawmakers to seek FDA action
item.description: Some patients and doctors are calling on the FDA to formally recognize a shortage of the medications, saying the agency's shortage database does not reflect problems they are seeing at pharmacies.

item.title: Trump $1 coins are now on sale. Here's how much they cost.
item.description: The U.S. Mint said the President Donald J. Trump $1 coin can be bought in packages of 25 for $61 or 100 coins for $154.50.

item.title: Watch live: Suspect in downtown Minneapolis mass shooting was facing eviction
item.description: The man suspected of killing two people and injuring six others in a mass shooting at a downtown Minneapolis apartment complex Wednesday was facing eviction after a string of incidents including assault and allegedly showing a gun to apartment management, according to court documents.

item.title: Hegseth favors Sean Parnell for Army secretary, sources say
item.description: Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth has told people close to him that Sean Parnell would be his top choice for secretary of the Army, several senior officials told CBS News.

item.title: New details emerge on deadly Minneapolis apartment shooting
item.description: New details are emerging on the shooting in Minneapolis that killed two people and left more injured. CBS News' Jonah Kaplan has the latest.

item.title: The Social Security Administration overpaid her. Now she owes $35,000.
item.description: The agency told a woman that she has 30 days to pay them back. Otherwise, it would cut her benefits by 50% while it collects what it overpaid.

item.title: Tillis slams Hegseth's priorities, urges Trump to remove him as defense secretary
item.description: Republican Sen. Thom Tillis of South Carolina urged President Trump to remove Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth amid a series of high-profile exits from the agency. CBS News' Nikole Killion has more.

item.title: Ross Fire still burning, with over 90,000 acres scorched
item.description: The wildfire, which has torn through Palo Pinto and Jack counties, has forced evacuations, closed roads and disrupted schools.

item.title: Why New York City is temporarily banning AI in most public school classrooms
item.description: New York City Public Schools is banning the use of artificial intelligence in most classrooms for the next year. New York City Councilman Eric Dinowitz joins with more.

item.title: Should you delay veterinary care because of cost?
item.description: Rising veterinary costs are forcing pet owners to make tough decisions, but should delaying care be one of them?

item.title: Postal Service mail voting rules face extended block as judge presses DOJ
item.description: A federal judge is considering whether to continue blocking a U.S. Postal Service rule imposing new requirements for mail voting.

item.title: Audio of emergency call for plane carrying DHS chief as it experienced engine failure
item.description: A Coast Guard plane carrying Department of Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin and other top officials made an emergency landing Wednesday at Ronald Reagan Washington National Airport, after an engine failure. CBS News' Nicole Sganga has more.

item.title: DOJ charges ICE officer who shot immigrant with lying to investigators
item.description: Federal prosecutors have charged an ICE officer who shot a Venezuelan immigrant in Minnesota with making false statements about the incident, sources said.

item.title: "Supersized" El Niño's harshest weather ahead includes heat, drought, floods
item.description: A new forecast predicts with almost 100% certainty that El Niño will remain in place until early 2027, peaking later this year.

item.title: Chocolate eyeball candy sold at Marshalls, TJ Maxx recalled
item.description: The recalled candy, sold under the brand "Crystal Temptations," was distributed in 13 states.

item.title: Lindsay Clancy jury deadlocked as judge gives "dynamite" instruction
item.description: The jury in the Lindsay Clancy murder trial will resume deliberations Thursday, a day after getting a final "dynamite" instruction from the judge.

item.title: The Secret Lies in the Gut
item.description: Laurie Cox spends her day investigating the role of the gut microbiota in neurologic diseases like Alzheimer's and Parkinson's. This week, she joins Norah to discuss the role the gut microbiome plays in aging and disease, and why her work could lead to more personalized medicine as we learn more about the connection between the gut, hormones and women's health. Plus, Norah shares what she eats in the morning to jumpstart her gut!

item.title: Estrogen, Testosterone and Menopause, Oh My!
item.description: This week on Healthful, urologist and sexual medicine specialist Dr. Rachel Rubin discusses how female bodies change during perimenopause and menopause — and explains why women may be suffering unnecessarily. Dr. Rubin and Norah discuss how vaginal hormones could save Medicare between $6 and $22 billion a year and even prevent urinary tract infections. Plus, Norah reveals her experience with menopause and hormone replacement therapy.

item.title: The Truth About Postpartum Psychosis
item.description: The issue of postpartum psychosis has come to the forefront amid the murder trial of Lindsay Clancy, the 35-year-old mother accused of killing her three children. What are the signs of a mental break, and is the healthcare system failing mothers? In this special episode of Healthful, Norah speaks with Dr. Uruj Kamal Haider, a perinatal psychiatrist who has treated patients with the rare and severe mental health emergency. She also speaks with Kriti Lodha, a postpartum psychosis survivor who has made it her mission to help other mothers.

item.title: Reclaiming History: Inside the 60 Minutes story as it unfolded in real time
item.description: Watch as the Miller family discovers the slave cemetery at Sharswood, a former plantation, where their enslaved ancestors were likely buried.
